page.layout: One page of text in one column, with a centred title and a table below it, two number columns with a label between them, and a catchword at lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: tuit ipsius dolus, qui appellationem Dei ad solam Patris personam restringere confevisset: in qua tamen teterrima blasphemia vir pessimus perseverans, rogante Dominum tota quae adstabat Ecclesia, ut eius animum immutaret, & nobis hominem assidue ad resipiscentiam hortantibus, tandem justo Dei judicio caesus, blasphemare simul & viuere in hoc mundo desiit.

Habes, pie lector, historiae diffusae breuem & veram explicationem. Tu nobiscum Deum æternum invoca, ut tanta scandala ab Ecclesia sua clementer avertat, populo suo largiatur vigilantes & idoneos ministros, qui serio ament διδασκαλίαν ὑγιαινούσαν, ἀντιλέγοντας [?] utiliter possint ἐλέγχειν: universum autem veritatis sermone norint ὀρθοτομεῖν ad nominis sui gloriam, & Ecclesiae utilitatem per Jesum Christum Filium eius unicum & coæternum, Amen.
main_text.head: Quando vixerint & floruerint scriptores Ecclesiastici, quos patres appellamus.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word of the page, "tuit", is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The Greek accents and breathings are uncertain; ἀντιλέγοντας is marked [?]. The year 445 and 405 are printed in this order, as in the scan. The table's middle label "Vixit anno Domini" runs down beside rows 7 to 9; it is set as one cell per row. The letters ue/uei in "confueuisset" were read as a consonant v before e and i (confevisset). The heading and table are italic and centred on the scan; the Latin in the table is roman.
